chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ala', who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I performed Tamattu', slaughtered the sacrifice, and shaved my head; should I apply henna to my head? He said: 'Yes, provided you do not touch any perfume.' I said: Should I wear the qamis (shirt)? He said: 'Yes, if you wish.' I said: Should I cover my head? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعْتُ: I performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What actions are permissible for a pilgrim after shaving their head during Umrah or Hajj while still in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the gradual release from Ihram restrictions for a Mutamatti', specifically addressing the permissibility of grooming acts like applying henna and wearing a shirt immediately after the sacrifice and head shaving. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the prohibition of perfume (which remains strict until full release) and the allowance of clothing and head covering, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding the transition from the sacred state to normalcy.
